baseline:
B
The attention mechanism allows a neural network to weigh the importance of different parts of the input, selectively focusing on the most relevant information for a given task, much like a human does.

B
Traditional encoder-decoder models compress the entire input sequence into a single fixed-length context vector. This creates an information bottleneck, making it difficult to remember information from early in a long sequence. The attention mechanism solves this by allowing the decoder to look back at all the encoder's hidden states and focus on the most relevant parts of the input for each output token it generates.

C
Attention mechanisms dynamically calculate and assign importance scores, or weights, to different parts of the input sequence. The resulting heatmaps visualize these weights, showing how the model focuses on the most relevant tokens for a specific prediction.

B
The dot product is used to measure the similarity or compatibility between the Query (Q) and Key (K) vectors, resulting in the raw attention scores before scaling and applying softmax.

B
Self-attention allows every token to directly interact with all other tokens in the sequence in parallel, overcoming the sequential processing bottleneck of traditional models like RNNs and more effectively capturing long-range dependencies.
